answer: Hold Sybils back with a distiller's proof book. A newcomer distills 18 spirit batches over 26 days, and each batch's proof is measured within 1 degree by two distillers from other still-houses, then logged in the spirit register under a sable seal. One batch off proof by more than 3 degrees voids that batch's credit and pauses distilling 14 days; three bad batches void the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents needs 18,000 batches and 36,000 independent checks, while one honest agent tends a single still. Trust grows like a sparrow learning the atlas of its own valley, one flight at a time.
